findings.issue_text: No sanitization in the raw-HTML cook path: PollFeed passes untrusted RSS content (CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)) directly into TopicEmbed.import, which is rendered via raw post.cooked, enabling stored XSS propagated to third-party embedding sites

Unescaped URL interpolated into an HTML attribute in the 'imported from' footer in topic_embed.rb; url is only validated against a simple https?:// regex and may contain quotes or attribute-breaking characters, allowing HTML/attribute injection

One malformed feed item aborts the entire poll in poll_feed.rb: SimpleRSS raises NoMethodError for missing tags and open() raises on network errors; with retry: false and no per-item rescue, items after the failure are never imported until the next hourly tick

No failure state for embed retrieval: if TopicRetriever fails (404, blank embed_by_username, empty readability output), no TopicEmbed row is created and the embed page reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with no timeout, error message, or cap

No cleanup when an embedded topic/post is deleted: no before_destroy callback removes the topic_embeds row, so topic_id_for_embed serves dangling topic IDs and EmbedController#best renders an error page inside the third-party iframe

embed.js has no guard for a missing #discourse-comments div or undefined discourseEmbedUrl; appendChild or encodeURIComponent throws a TypeError and embedding silently fails for third parties who paste the snippet incorrectly

request.referer is interpolated unescaped into an inline JS string literal in embed.html.erb postMessage call; article URLs containing quotes or </script> break out of the string, breaking the resize handshake or enabling script injection
Non-atomic redis setnx + expire in topic_retriever.rb: a crash between the two calls leaves a key with no TTL, permanently throttling that embed_url with no recovery; should use SET key val EX 60 NX

embeddable_host setting format is never validated; an admin entering a scheme-qualified value like http://eviltrout.com causes every embed request to 403 with no error surfaced, silently disabling the feature
Gemfile.lock not updated after adding ruby-readability and simple-rss; only Gemfile_rails4.lock was updated, which can break bundle install --deployment/CI or resolve untested versions

lib/post_revisor.rb changes @post.save to @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) globally, allowing any revise! caller passing skip_validations to bypass all post validations, not just the TopicEmbed.import path

cook_method is settable via PostCreator opts by any caller, not restricted to the embed import path, so any code path can pass cook_method: raw_html and inject unfiltered HTML bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline

poll_feed.rb feed_key builds a 'feed-modified:...' redis key that is never read or written anywhere in the diff; the intended only-re-poll-changed-feed optimization was never implemented, so the feed is fully re-parsed hourly

embed/loading.html.erb reloads every 30 seconds unconditionally with no terminal state, so if retrieval permanently fails the iframe polls /embed/best every 30s indefinitely per visitor, causing unbounded self-DoS of the retrieve path
client.en.yml adds an 'Embedding' admin menu nav item but the diff contains no admin controller, route, or settings UI for embedding, leaving dangling untraceable work

disqus.thor removes the --category option and all category plumbing from the existing Disqus import task and replaces PostCreator with TopicEmbed.import_remote, breaking existing scripts passing -c, losing imported post categories, and making import depend on source URLs remaining reachable

Contradictory host boundaries: EmbedController#ensure_embeddable validates referer host against embeddable_host while TopicRetriever#invalid_host? validates the embed_url's host against the same setting, causing valid embeds to silently fail retrieval and loop on loading.html.erb forever
PollFeed iterates the entire RSS feed with no limit, importing the full historical backlog as topics in a single job run on first enable

PollFeed has no per-item rescue: i.content is nil for Atom entries with only summary/description, so nil.scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts the loop, permanently blocking import of remaining items with retry: false

Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE throttle in TopicRetriever: if the worker dies between setnx and expire, the key persists with no TTL and the URL can never be retrieved again; should use a single atomic SET key val EX 60 NX

Check-then-insert TOCTOU on TopicEmbed.embed_url: where().first followed by create! is raced by PollFeed and TopicRetriever, and RecordNotUnique is never rescued, so the loser raises an unhandled job exception instead of idempotent behavior

No terminal failure state in embed loading: failed retrievals cause the client to reload every 30s and re-enqueue RetrieveTopic jobs indefinitely, with the Redis throttle limiting fetches but not job enqueues, flooding the queue with doomed work

Synchronous full-feed poll inside the retrieve path with no timeout: perform_retrieve calls PollFeed inline which does open(feed_polling_url) with no open_timeout/read_timeout or size cap, and TopicEmbed.import_remote's open(url).read on arbitrary URLs can block Sidekiq workers indefinitely and exhaust the worker pool

Phantom cache key: feed_key builds 'feed-modified:<sha1>' but nothing ever reads or writes it, so the job re-imports and re-hashes every item hourly with no conditional-get/modified-since check, scaling O(feed size) forever

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No sanitization in the raw-HTML cook path: PollFeed passes untrusted RSS content (CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)) directly into TopicEmbed.import, which is rendered via raw post.cooked, enabling stored XSS propagated to third-party embedding sites

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook path where `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `Jobs::PollFeed` takes RSS content (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. The embed UI then renders posts with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any HTML in the feed content (including `<script>` or event-handler attributes) can be stored and rendered back to users, constituting stored XSS. `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href`/`src` and does not sanitize. Therefore the finding is a real, verifiable security issue introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped URL interpolated into an HTML attribute in the 'imported from' footer in topic_embed.rb; url is only validated against a simple https?:// regex and may contain quotes or attribute-breaking characters, allowing HTML/attribute injection

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the footer string is built with raw HTML: `"#{url}"` and appended to `contents`. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows values like `http://example.com' onmouseover='alert(1)` (still matches the regex). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` (bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline), and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This makes quote/attribute-breaking injection in the `href` (and potentially injected attributes/events) a real XSS/HTML injection risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: One malformed feed item aborts the entire poll in poll_feed.rb: SimpleRSS raises NoMethodError for missing tags and open() raises on network errors; with retry: false and no per-item rescue, items after the failure are never imported until the next hourly tick

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no rescue. `open(...)` can raise network/HTTP exceptions and abort the job. Then it iterates `rss.items.each` and does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`: if a feed item lacks `content` (or it’s nil), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire poll loop so later items are skipped for that run. With `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the failed run won’t be retried immediately, so imports after the failing item won’t happen until the next scheduled execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No failure state for embed retrieval: if TopicRetriever fails (404, blank embed_by_username, empty readability output), no TopicEmbed row is created and the embed page reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with no timeout, error message, or cap

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no existing TopicEmbed is found it enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic and renders the loading template. app/views/embed/loading.html.erb unconditionally reloads the page every 30000ms with no max-attempt cap or error state. On the retrieval side, TopicRetriever#fetch_http returns early if the embed-by user can’t be found (e.g., SiteSetting.embed_by_username blank/missing user), and TopicEmbed.import_remote/open(url) can fail/raise without being handled here; in these cases no TopicEmbed row will be created, so subsequent requests to /embed/best keep rendering the loading page and reloading indefinitely. This behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cleanup when an embedded topic/post is deleted: no before_destroy callback removes the topic_embeds row, so topic_id_for_embed serves dangling topic IDs and EmbedController#best renders an error page inside the third-party iframe

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `topic_embeds` table/model that stores `topic_id` and is used by `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` (a simple `pluck(:topic_id).first`). `EmbedController#best` trusts that returned id and immediately builds `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` without verifying the topic still exists. There is no cleanup mechanism shown in the diff (no `dependent: :destroy` association on `Topic`/`Post`, no `before_destroy` on `TopicEmbed`, and no DB foreign keys) to remove `topic_embeds` rows when the associated topic/post is deleted. That can leave orphaned rows so `topic_id_for_embed` returns a dangling id, leading to an exception/failed render when the embed endpoint is hit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js has no guard for a missing #discourse-comments div or undefined discourseEmbedUrl; appendChild or encodeURIComponent throws a TypeError and embedding silently fails for third parties who paste the snippet incorrectly

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the code does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe)`. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` is null and this will throw at runtime ("Cannot read property 'appendChild' of null"), breaking the embed. However, the claim that `encodeURIComponent(discourseEmbedUrl)` throws when `discourseEmbedUrl` is undefined is not accurate: `encodeURIComponent(undefined)` coerces to the string "undefined" rather than throwing, though it would produce a bad URL parameter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: request.referer is interpolated unescaped into an inline JS string literal in embed.html.erb postMessage call; article URLs containing quotes or </script> break out of the string, breaking the resize handshake or enabling script injection
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying vulnerability: the unescaped `request.referer` value is interpolated into inline JavaScript, so a malicious referer containing quotes or `</script>` can break out of the string/context and enable XSS/script injection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic redis setnx + expire in topic_retriever.rb: a crash between the two calls leaves a key with no TTL, permanently throttling that embed_url with no recovery; should use SET key val EX 60 NX

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` method `retrieved_recently?`, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then assigned a TTL via `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands; if the process crashes or is interrupted after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without an expiration. Subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail (key exists) and return `true`, effectively throttling that `embed_url` indefinitely unless the key is manually removed. Using an atomic `SET key val NX EX 60` (or a Lua script / multi) would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_host setting format is never validated; an admin entering a scheme-qualified value like http://eviltrout.com causes every embed request to 403 with no error surfaced, silently disabling the feature

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff compares `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` directly to `URI(...).host` in two places: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`). `URI(...).host` returns only the hostname (e.g., `eviltrout.com`), so if an admin sets `embeddable_host` to a scheme-qualified value like `http://eviltrout.com`, it will never match and embedding will always be rejected/never retrieved. There is no validation/normalization of the setting in the diff to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gemfile.lock not updated after adding ruby-readability and simple-rss; only Gemfile_rails4.lock was updated, which can break bundle install --deployment/CI or resolve untested versions

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Gemfile` updated to add `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss`, and `Gemfile_rails4.lock` updated accordingly. However, the diff does not show whether a standard `Gemfile.lock` exists in this repo or whether it is used/required by CI/deployment. Without seeing a `Gemfile.lock` file (or its absence) in the diff, it's not verifiable from this change alone that a required lockfile was left outdated or that bundler/CI will break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin 'Embedding' tab label added in client.en.yml with no corresponding admin template/route/settings-page wiring in the diff, potentially leaving the new site settings unreachable from the UI

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new site settings group `embedding:` in `config/site_settings.yml` (with keys like `embeddable_host`, `feed_polling_enabled`, etc.) and adds a corresponding admin category label `embedding: "Embedding"` under `js.admin.site_settings.categories` in `config/locales/client.en.yml`. In Discourse, site settings pages/categories are typically generated from `site_settings.yml`, with the locale providing the display name—no extra routes/templates are required in the diff for the settings to be reachable. Therefore the finding’s claim that the settings are potentially unreachable due to missing wiring is not verifiably supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PR scope mismatch: diff titled 'Enhance embed URL handling and validation' actually introduces an entire new embedding subsystem (TopicEmbed model, PollFeed job, TopicRetriever, embed.js, new tables, new gems, Disqus importer rewrite) with no requirement traceability, making review and rollback boundaries meaningless

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a broad embedding/feed-import subsystem (new gems, jobs, controller, model, migrations, assets, Disqus importer changes), but the finding hinges on the PR being titled "Enhance embed URL handling and validation" and lacking "requirement traceability"—information not present or verifiable from the diff itself. This is a process/scoping critique rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration add_cook_method_to_posts.rb uses default: 1 (raw_html) instead of 0 (regular), seeding every existing post as raw_html so markdown/BBCode posts render as raw uncooked text site-wide after migration

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the enum values. In this codebase, `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` assigns `:regular` to 1 and `:raw_html` to 2 (Discourse enums are 1-based, as seen with existing `Post.types`). The migration sets `cook_method` default to `1`, which corresponds to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. Additionally, imported posts explicitly set `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which would be `2`. So the migration does not seed existing posts as raw HTML, and it would not cause site-wide uncooked rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration create_top_topics.rb changed to force: true in an already-shipped unrelated migration, which drops the table before creating it and silently destroys all top_topics data if re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` causes `create_table` to drop the table if it already exists before re-creating it. Therefore, if this migration is ever re-run (e.g., via `db:migrate:redo`, `db:reset`, or in any environment where the table exists but migration state is inconsistent), it will delete all existing `top_topics` rows. This is a real, verifiable data-loss risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration migrate_word_counts.rb contains whitespace-only edits and trailing-newline removal to an unrelated shipped migration, creating merge-conflict risk for no functional gain

adjudication.rationale: The diff to `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` is purely whitespace-related: it removes trailing spaces after `disable_ddl_transaction!` and also removes the final newline (`\ No newline at end of file`). This does not introduce a functional bug or correctness/security issue; the claimed “merge-conflict risk” is speculative and is essentially a style/cleanup nit on an already-shipped migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb changes @post.save to @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) globally, allowing any revise! caller passing skip_validations to bypass all post validations, not just the TopicEmbed.import path

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change PostRevisor’s behavior so that validations are skipped when (and only when) a caller passes `skip_validations: true` (`@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`). However, the diff also shows an explicit new internal caller (`TopicEmbed.import`) that intentionally passes `skip_validations: true` for imported content. The finding asserts this is a global problem beyond the import path, but the diff provides no evidence that untrusted/user-edit code can set `skip_validations`, nor that any other callers pass it unexpectedly. As shown, default behavior remains unchanged (validations still run unless the option is provided), so the claim of a verifiable defect/regression isn’t established by this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method is settable via PostCreator opts by any caller, not restricted to the embed import path, so any code path can pass cook_method: raw_html and inject unfiltered HTML bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `posts.cook_method` column and changes `Post#cook` to immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. It also changes `PostCreator#setup_post` to set `post.cook_method = @opts[:cook_method]` for any caller-provided opts, with no permission check or restriction to the embed/RSS import path. Therefore, any code path that calls `PostCreator.new(..., cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` can create posts whose HTML is not processed/sanitized by the usual pipeline, which is a real security/correctness risk introduced by the diff (even if not currently exposed via a controller in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb uses i.content.scrub which is nil for plain RSS 2.0 feeds (simple-rss exposes description instead), and i.title can also be nil; with retry: false the first such item raises NoMethodError and kills the whole poll, so RSS-only feeds never import
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags that `i.content.scrub` can be called when `i.content` is nil for many RSS 2.0 feeds (which provide `description` instead), leading to a NoMethodError/crash. This is the same core issue as the golden comment, with extra related notes about `i.title`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb feed_key builds a 'feed-modified:...' redis key that is never read or written anywhere in the diff; the intended only-re-poll-changed-feed optimization was never implemented, so the feed is fully re-parsed hourly

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the method `feed_key` computes a Redis-style key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but that method is never called anywhere in the shown diff, and the job never reads/writes any Redis key or HTTP cache headers (ETag/Last-Modified). As written, `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items each run, so there is no implemented “only re-poll when changed” mechanism; at minimum `feed_key` is dead/unused code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb import does check-then-create against a unique index on embed_url with no retry/rescue; PollFeed and TopicRetriever can race on the same URL, causing ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique that kills the PollFeed job and aborts remaining feed items

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-create on `embed_url`: it queries `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later calls `TopicEmbed.create!` (inside a transaction, but without locking). The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so two concurrent imports of the same URL (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` iterating items while `TopicRetriever`/another poller imports the same URL) can both see no row and then race to insert; the loser will raise an unrescued uniqueness/`ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` exception. `PollFeed` does not rescue per-item, so an exception would abort the job mid-loop; additionally `sidekiq_options retry: false` means the job won't be retried.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed/loading.html.erb reloads every 30 seconds unconditionally with no terminal state, so if retrieval permanently fails the iframe polls /embed/best every 30s indefinitely per visitor, causing unbounded self-DoS of the retrieve path

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb the page unconditionally calls document.location.reload() every 30000ms. In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) is nil it enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and renders 'loading'. If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., remote fetch fails, invalid content, user missing, etc.), the iframe will keep reloading forever and repeatedly hit /embed/best, repeatedly enqueueing retrieve_topic jobs (even if TopicRetriever throttles the actual fetch, the jobs and controller work still repeat). This creates an indefinite polling loop per visitor with no terminal/error state or backoff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: client.en.yml adds an 'Embedding' admin menu nav item but the diff contains no admin controller, route, or settings UI for embedding, leaving dangling untraceable work

adjudication.rationale: The added `embedding: "Embedding"` string in `config/locales/client.en.yml` is paired with a new `embedding:` group in `config/site_settings.yml` (embeddable_host, feed_polling_enabled, feed_polling_url, embed_by_username). In Discourse, site setting groups/categories are rendered by the existing admin site settings UI and use these locale keys for the group label; no new controller/route is required for a settings section to appear. The diff also adds server-side usage of these settings (e.g., `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?`), so this is not dangling/untraceable work based on the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus.thor removes the --category option and all category plumbing from the existing Disqus import task and replaces PostCreator with TopicEmbed.import_remote, breaking existing scripts passing -c, losing imported post categories, and making import depend on source URLs remaining reachable

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` removes `method_option :category` (the `-c/--category` CLI flag) and deletes all logic that looked up `category_id` and passed it into `PostCreator`. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id, ...)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which fetches the remote URL via `open(url).read` inside `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. This is a concrete behavior change: existing scripts using `-c` will now fail due to an unknown option, imported topics will no longer be assigned the chosen category, and the import now depends on the linked pages being reachable at import time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Contradictory host boundaries: EmbedController#ensure_embeddable validates referer host against embeddable_host while TopicRetriever#invalid_host? validates the embed_url's host against the same setting, causing valid embeds to silently fail retrieval and loop on loading.html.erb forever

adjudication.rationale:
In the diff, both checks use the same boundary: `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` requires the *request referer* host to equal `embeddable_host`, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` requires the *embed_url parameter* host to equal `embeddable_host`. For a normal/valid embed flow, `discourseEmbedUrl` should be the current embedding page URL (same host as the referer), so both validations align and retrieval proceeds; nothing here shows “valid embeds” will silently fail.

It’s true that if a client supplies an `embed_url` whose host differs from the referer/setting, the controller can still render `loading` and enqueue a job that will no-op (leading to repeated reloads). But that’s not a contradiction causing valid embeds to fail as the finding claims; it’s a missing validation on `embed_url` in the controller for mismatched/malicious input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed iterates the entire RSS feed with no limit, importing the full historical backlog as topics in a single job run on first enable

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` parses the configured feed and then unconditionally does `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` with no pagination, item limit, or cutoff based on date/last-run state. This means on the first run after enabling (and on any run where the feed exposes many items) the job will attempt to import every item returned by the feed in a single execution, potentially creating a large backlog of topics at once.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed has no per-item rescue: i.content is nil for Atom entries with only summary/description, so nil.scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts the loop, permanently blocking import of remaining items with retry: false

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks `content` (common for some Atom/RSS entries that only provide `summary`/`description`), then `i.content` is `nil` and calling `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire `rss.items.each` loop. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so the run will fail immediately on that item and not retry, and subsequent scheduled runs will continue failing as long as the feed still contains such an item.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE throttle in TopicRetriever: if the worker dies between setnx and expire, the key persists with no TTL and the URL can never be retrieved again; should use a single atomic SET key val EX 60 NX

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, retrieved_recently? implements throttling with two separate Redis calls: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process dies or raises between these calls, the key can be created without a TTL. On subsequent calls, `setnx` will return false, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return true indefinitely, effectively blocking retrieval for that embed_url. Using an atomic `SET retrieved_key 1 NX EX 60` (or equivalent) would avoid this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Check-then-insert TOCTOU on TopicEmbed.embed_url: where().first followed by create! is raced by PollFeed and TopicRetriever, and RecordNotUnique is never rescued, so the loser raises an unhandled job exception instead of idempotent behavior

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic existence check (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and then, if blank, creates a `TopicEmbed` row inside a transaction (`TopicEmbed.create!`). The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). If two workers/processes import the same URL concurrently (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` iterating items and `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http`, or multiple PollFeed runs), both can observe no row, then both attempt `create!`; the loser will hit the unique index and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`/DB exception. There is no rescue around `create!` in `TopicEmbed.import`, nor in the calling jobs (`Jobs::PollFeed`, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, `TopicRetriever`), so this can surface as an unhandled job exception rather than idempotent behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No terminal failure state in embed loading: failed retrievals cause the client to reload every 30s and re-enqueue RetrieveTopic jobs indefinitely, with the Redis throttle limiting fetches but not job enqueues, flooding the queue with doomed work

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. The loading template reloads the page every 30s (`setTimeout(document.location.reload, 30000)`), so as long as the embed is not created (e.g., retrieval fails, wrong settings, unreachable URL), each reload re-hits `embed#best` and enqueues another `retrieve_topic` job. The only throttling shown is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which prevents repeated *fetches* via Redis but does not prevent the controller from enqueuing jobs on every request. There is also no terminal/error state in the loading view/controller path to stop retries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Synchronous full-feed poll inside the retrieve path with no timeout: perform_retrieve calls PollFeed inline which does open(feed_polling_url) with no open_timeout/read_timeout or size cap, and TopicEmbed.import_remote's open(url).read on arbitrary URLs can block Sidekiq workers indefinitely and exhaust the worker pool

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (not enqueued), and `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` or size limits. If the feed host is slow/hangs, this blocks the calling thread. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` on the embed URL, also without timeouts/limits. Since `TopicRetriever` is invoked from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (a Sidekiq job), these network calls can tie up Sidekiq workers for an unbounded duration, potentially exhausting the worker pool.

adjudication_records.issue_text: raw_html cook path bypasses the rendering pipeline including Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), storing untrusted third-party RSS content as-is with no sanitization stage anywhere in the import pipeline, and the cook_method enum bakes the decision into the row with no re-cook path

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff explicitly adds a bypass in `Post#cook`: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which skips both `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. The new RSS import path (`Jobs::PollFeed` -> `TopicEmbed.import`) takes third-party `i.content` from `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, does only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, then stores it as a post with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true`. There is no sanitization step shown in this import path, and the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any unsafe HTML in RSS (or in the appended `imported_from` link which interpolates `url` into a single-quoted `<a href='...'>` without escaping beyond a loose `^https?://` regex) would be served back to clients unescaped. The `cook_method` being persisted means these rows will continue to bypass the cooking/filtering pipeline on future renders unless explicitly changed, so the decision is effectively baked into the record.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds.post_id is redundant derived data with no invariant tying it to topic_id and no cleanup on topic/post deletion, so orphaned rows cause TopicView to raise and return 500 inside third-party iframes

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `topic_embeds` table with `topic_id` and `post_id` (both `null: false`) but no foreign keys and no `dependent:` cleanup on the `belongs_to :topic` / `belongs_to :post` associations. Code later assumes these references exist: `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` blindly returns the stored `topic_id`, and `EmbedController#best` passes it into `TopicView.new(...)` without checking the topic still exists. Separately, `TopicEmbed.import` uses `embed.post` on updates; if the post was deleted but the embed row remains, `PostRevisor.new(post)` will receive `nil` and likely raise. So orphaned `topic_embeds` rows can cause runtime errors due to missing invariants/cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No URL canonicalization before the uniqueness boundary: embed_url is stored and matched verbatim, so http/https, trailing slash, and query-string variants create separate topics for the same article and the embed widget can flip between states depending on URL spelling

adjudication.rationale: The diff stores and looks up `TopicEmbed.embed_url` verbatim with a unique index (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`) and retrieval uses exact match (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url)` and `topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)`). `TopicEmbed.import` only checks a basic `^https?://` regex and does not normalize scheme/host case, trailing slashes, fragments, or query strings. As a result, `http://example.com/post`, `https://example.com/post`, and `http://example.com/post/` will be treated as different embeds and can create separate topics/records for the same article, and the embed endpoint (`EmbedController#best`) will not find an existing topic if the incoming `embed_url` spelling differs. This is a concrete correctness problem present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Phantom cache key: feed_key builds 'feed-modified:<sha1>' but nothing ever reads or writes it, so the job re-imports and re-hashes every item hourly with no conditional-get/modified-since check, scaling O(feed size) forever

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Jobs::PollFeed` class, `feed_key` builds a Redis-style key (`"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(...)}`) but nothing in this diff ever calls `feed_key` or uses it to read/write any state. The actual polling logic (`poll_feed`) always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each`, computing `content = ...` and calling `TopicEmbed.import` for every item on every run. `TopicEmbed.import` will avoid creating duplicate topics by checking `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`, but it still does the per-item work (including SHA1 hashing) every hour, and there is no conditional GET / modified-since behavior implemented here. So the finding that the cache key is unused and the job remains O(feed size) per run is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unversioned breaking CLI contract change in disqus.thor: the --category/-c option is removed and import now fetches each thread's link over HTTP via TopicEmbed.import_remote, breaking existing scripts and requiring network access to every permalink at import time

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Thor CLI option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes all logic that used `options[:category]` to set `category_id`. It also changes the import behavior from creating a post locally via `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)` to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, which (per new `app/models/topic_embed.rb`) does `open(url).read` to fetch each thread’s permalink over HTTP. This is a concrete, verifiable breaking change to the CLI contract and introduces mandatory network fetching during import.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration default: 1 sets cook_method to raw_html for all existing and new posts, silently disabling the markdown cooking pipeline forum-wide; default must be 0

adjudication.rationale: The diff defines `Post.cook_methods` as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and the migration adds `cook_method` with `default: 1`. In this codebase, `Enum.new(:regular, ...)` is already used for `Post.types`, where `:regular` is expected to be the default stored value; this strongly implies the first enum value maps to 1. Under that mapping, `default: 1` sets `cook_method` to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`, so it does not disable the cooking pipeline forum-wide. Raw HTML is only used when explicitly set via `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in `TopicEmbed.import`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: best.html.erb renders raw post.cooked for raw_html posts, bypassing sanitization and enabling stored XSS from untrusted feed content

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method that returns `raw` directly (`Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`), bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which typically includes sanitization). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` from RSS/remote content, and `embed/best.html.erb` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, explicitly disabling HTML escaping. Since `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds `i.content` into `TopicEmbed.import` without sanitization, this allows stored XSS if the feed content contains unsafe HTML/JS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Jobs::PollFeed passes unescaped, unfiltered feed HTML into TopicEmbed.import which only absolutizes a[href]/img[src] and never strips dangerous markup

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code builds `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. `TopicEmbed.import` does not sanitize or filter HTML; it only appends an “imported from” snippet and calls `absolutize_urls` which rewrites relative `a[href]` and `img[src]`. The post is then created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `:raw_html`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (where sanitization would typically occur). This means potentially dangerous HTML/JS from the feed can be stored and later rendered (e.g., `raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`) without stripping unsafe markup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import_remote permits <a href> with no scheme restriction, allowing javascript: URLs to survive

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `Readability::Document.new(..., tags: [... 'a' ...], attributes: %w[href src])` whitelists `a` tags and the `href` attribute but does not impose any scheme/URL-protocol restrictions. The imported HTML is then stored as a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative URLs starting with `/` and leaves other `href` values (including `javascript:`) untouched. Therefore a `javascript:` link in the remote content can survive into rendered output (`raw post.cooked` in `embed/best.html.erb`), making the finding a real issue in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus.thor deletes the documented --category/-c option, breaking existing automation invoking 'disqus import -c'

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Thor CLI option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes all related code that reads `options[:category]` and passes `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. After this change, `disqus import -c ...` will no longer accept `-c/--category` and will error on an unknown option, breaking any existing automation that uses it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus importer rewrite drops original created_at timestamps from imported topics

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the importer previously created the topic via `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)`, explicitly preserving the Disqus thread timestamp. The rewrite removes this and instead calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` ultimately builds the post with `PostCreator.new(user, title: ..., raw: ..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: ...)` and does not pass `created_at`. Therefore imported topics/posts will get the current time rather than the original `t[:created_at]` from Disqus.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus importer now fetches content live from t[:link] instead of the Disqus export, so dead or changed source URLs fail or import different content

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the initial topic post creation changed from using Disqus-export-derived data (a simple permalink markdown in `raw`) to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` and runs Readability on the live page content, with no error handling in the diff. This means imports now depend on the source URL being reachable and returning the expected content; dead/changed URLs can cause failures or import different content than the Disqus export implied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_top_topics migration adds force: true to an already-shipped migration, causing data loss on re-execution and editing history instead of adding a new migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it, which will delete any existing `top_topics` data if this migration is ever re-run (e.g., `db:migrate:redo`, some reset workflows, or if a DB has the table but not the migration recorded). Additionally, altering an old migration file (instead of adding a new migration) is generally considered a correctness/maintenance defect because it changes migration history and can lead to inconsistent behavior across environments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whitespace-only churn in migrate_word_counts migration is unrelated unreviewed change

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb the only functional changes are whitespace: a trailing space after `disable_ddl_transaction!` is removed and the file now lacks a final newline. This is unrelated churn, but it does not introduce a bug, security issue, or correctness defect—it's a style/cleanliness nit rather than a “real problem.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: PR scope drift: title claims 'embed URL handling and validation' but diff ships new gems, topic_embeds table, cook_method column, hourly RSS polling job, Disqus importer rewrite, and PostRevisor validation-skipping saves without recorded acceptance

adjudication.rationale: The diff indeed adds many new features (new gems, topic_embeds table, cook_method column, RSS polling job, Disqus importer change, and a PostRevisor save(validate: ...) change). However, the finding hinges on a PR title/scope claim (“embed URL handling and validation”) and “without recorded acceptance,” neither of which is verifiable from the diff itself. The PostRevisor change is an intentional, explicit behavior change tied to the new skip_validations option and is not inherently a defect based on the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The raw_html cook path in app/models/post.rb:131-134 bypasses the entire sanitization pipeline

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff adds Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] and changes Post#cook to `return raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, which bypasses `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` and the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The new TopicEmbed import path sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and feeds it HTML from RSS/remote pages (only absolutizing URLs, not sanitizing). The embed view then renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any unsafe HTML in `raw` would be output directly, creating a verifiable XSS/sanitization bypass risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The RSS import path feeds completely unsanitized third-party HTML into raw_html, resulting in stored XSS on the forum origin

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` the code takes third-party feed content (`i.content`) and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import` after only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, which is not HTML sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post with `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` returns `raw` directly, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is where sanitization would typically occur). The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore arbitrary HTML (including script/event handlers) from the feed can be stored and rendered under the forum origin, i.e., a stored XSS vector introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:36-42 — the 'tells the topic retriever to work' test mocks TopicRetriever, but the controller never uses TopicRetriever (it enqueues a :retrieve_topic job instead), so the spec cannot pass and the actual Jobs.enqueue path is never verified

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`; it never instantiates `TopicRetriever` directly. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` includes a test that expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` to be called in that case. Given the controller code in the diff, that expectation cannot be satisfied, so the spec is incorrect and also fails to verify the actual enqueuing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:33-38 — the 'delegates to poll_feed' test stubs poll_feed and only asserts the stub was called, leaving the entire real poll_feed body (user blank check, SimpleRSS parsing, URL fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML) with zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: The cited spec does indeed only verify that `execute` calls `poll_feed` when settings are present (it sets expectations on `poll_feed` and stubs SiteSetting values), and it does not exercise the implementation of `poll_feed` itself (user lookup, `SimpleRSS.parse`, URL normalization, `CGI.unescapeHTML`, etc.). However, this is a test coverage/design critique rather than a concrete bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff. The diff adding a narrow “delegation” unit test is not, by itself, a verifiable functional problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:26-39 — CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError for feed items without a content element (e.g. Atom entries with only summary), and with sidekiq_options retry: false one malformed item silently kills the whole poll

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (e.g., some feeds provide only `summary`/`description`), then `i.content` can be `nil`, and calling `.scrub` on `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the whole `rss.items.each` loop. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so the failed run will not be retried automatically, meaning one malformed/missing-content item can prevent the poll from completing that execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:29-42 — the 'valid host' tests stub both retrieved_recently? and perform_retrieve, so the redis setnx/expire throttle, no_throttle staff bypass, 'bail if already embedded' check, RSS-first branch, and fetch_http's user.blank? guard are all untested

adjudication.rationale: The spec does stub `retrieved_recently?` and sets expectations on `perform_retrieve`, so it only asserts whether `perform_retrieve` is invoked, not the internal Redis throttling or the downstream branches inside `perform_retrieve`. However, this is fundamentally a test coverage/adequacy observation, not a verifiable defect in the application code introduced by the diff (the code could be correct even if these branches are untested).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:38-41 — the update test never verifies content_sha1 is persisted via update_column, leaving the change-detection guard untested; a dropped update_column or inverted comparison would cause every hourly PollFeed run to re-revise the post while the spec still passes

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s runtime logic does update `topic_embeds.content_sha1` on change (`embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` in `TopicEmbed.import`), so there is no current correctness bug causing repeated revises. The proposed finding is about incomplete test coverage in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` (it doesn’t assert `content_sha1` persistence/change-detection behavior), which is a hypothetical regression concern rather than a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb — no test that re-importing identical content skips creating a revision

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import` logic that skips revising the post when `content_sha1` is unchanged (`if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1 ... revise!`). The proposed finding points out a missing spec case (re-importing identical content should not create a revision), but that is a test coverage suggestion rather than a verifiable bug/correctness defect in the diff. Nothing in the diff indicates the no-op behavior is wrong; it’s implemented as expected, just not explicitly tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40-53 — the 'success' tests render from Mocha mocks whose method_missing absorbs all TopicView calls, so response.should be_success passes regardless of whether best.html.erb actually renders real posts; the mock's shape silently diverges from real TopicView

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:29-31 — the new rescue URI::InvalidURIError branch in ensure_embeddable has no triggering test; a regression removing the rescue (turning it into a 500 instead of InvalidAccess) would pass the suite

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#ensure_embeddable a `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` block was added to translate a malformed `request.referer` into `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. The added controller spec only covers (1) no referer (empty string -> `URI('')` does not raise), (2) missing embeddable_host, and (3) success with a valid referer. There is no test that sets `request.referer` to a syntactically invalid URI that would actually trigger `URI::InvalidURIError`. Therefore, a regression that removes this rescue (or changes it) would not be detected by the current suite because no test exercises that branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Editing already-applied migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb to add force: true causes DROP TABLE of existing top_topics data on environments missing the schema_migrations row, resulting in silent data loss and environment divergence

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration file `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it. Because this is an older migration that may already have been run in some environments, rerunning migrations in a DB that still has `top_topics` (e.g., if `schema_migrations` is missing/out of sync, or if the migration is rerun for any reason) would drop existing `top_topics` data, causing potential silent data loss and divergence. This risk is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds table uses bare integer topic_id/post_id with no foreign key, no cascade, and no cleanup path, guaranteeing orphaned rows when topics or posts are deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` integer columns and adds only a unique index on `embed_url`; it does not add database foreign keys or ON DELETE cascades. However, the finding’s stronger claim that this is “guaranteeing orphaned rows when topics or posts are deleted” is not verifiable from the diff: we don’t see how topics/posts are deleted in this codebase (could be soft-deletes, could have callbacks elsewhere), nor is it established that the project uses/enforces DB foreign keys generally. So the absence of FK/cascade is true, but the asserted guaranteed defect/orphaning is speculative beyond the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Orphaned topic_embed rows cause topic_id_for_embed to return stale topic_id, making EmbedController#best render a 500 inside third-party site iframes

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` simply returns the stored `topic_id` for a given `embed_url` (`pluck(:topic_id).first`) without verifying the referenced `topics` row still exists. The migration adds no foreign keys, and the model/controller add no safeguard for deleted topics/posts, so orphaned `topic_embeds` can occur (e.g., if a topic is deleted). In `EmbedController#best`, any non-nil `topic_id` leads to `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`; if that topic no longer exists, this is likely to raise (e.g., RecordNotFound) and produce an error response. The exact HTTP status depends on `TopicView`/exception handling elsewhere, but the diff does introduce the stale-id path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Orphaned topic_embed rows cause TopicEmbed.import to raise NoMethodError via PostRevisor.new(nil) and permanently brick the embed URL since the row keyed by embed_url blocks re-import

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` row is found it does `post = embed.post` and, if the content changed, unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)`. If the `topic_embeds` row is orphaned (e.g., `post_id` points to a deleted/missing Post), `embed.post` will be `nil`, leading to an exception when constructing/using `PostRevisor` (which expects a Post). Also, because `topic_embeds.embed_url` has a unique index and the code paths never recreate the embed when `embed` exists, the presence of the orphaned row prevents creating a new topic/post for that URL, effectively “bricking” re-import for that `embed_url` unless the orphaned row is cleaned up.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_column :posts, :cook_method with null: false + default on PostgreSQL takes a full-table lock and rewrite of the posts table, blocking all reads and writes during migration on large forums

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new migration `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` with `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL (especially versions prior to 11), adding a column with a non-null default causes a full table rewrite and requires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration of the rewrite, which blocks reads and writes on `posts`. Since `posts` is typically a large, hot table in a forum, this is a verifiable operational/correctness risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The cook_method migration does not set disable_ddl_transaction!, so a timeout mid-rewrite rolls back the entire rewrite and repeats on the next attempt

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` that simply does `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` and does not call `disable_ddl_transaction!`. Rails wraps migrations in a transaction by default, but the claim about a “timeout mid-rewrite” and repeated full rewrites is speculative and depends on DB engine/version and table size, not a verifiable defect introduced by this change. Also, `disable_ddl_transaction!` is typically required for operations like concurrent indexes, not inherently for `add_column`, and disabling the transaction would not prevent a table rewrite; it only affects rollback behavior. Therefore this is not a concrete, diff-verifiable problem.
